subject: Commit spend holdback stagger & tax-jurisdiction checkpoints
messages:
From: Samantha Price <samantha.price@brightlane.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Cc: Marcus Reed <marcus.reed@brightlane.com>
Date: Sun, 14 Mar 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Annual prepay — multi-entity holdback & VAT timing

Jordan —

Thanks for the quick sync last week. Brightlane is finalizing the legal ops for our committed prepay (RDW-4721) and we need a tight invoice & drawdown plan that handles:
- multi-entity remit (US / EU / UK)
- holdback / milestone phasing across Q2–Q4
- VAT reclaim timing for the EU entity (we need clear windows so our reclaim team can plan)

Can you send a proposed invoicing cadence and the lockbox routing we discussed? We also attached our PO and VAT IDs for each entity (Brightlane_PO_and_tax_ids.pdf).

Target: invoice cadence by 3/18 so our AP can wire first tranche by 3/25.

Best,
Samantha Price
VP Finance, Brightlane
[sig] Brightlane | +1 415 555 0199

Attachments: Brightlane_PO_and_tax_ids.pdf (pdf)
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
To: Samantha Price <samantha.price@brightlane.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 15 Mar 2027 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Annual prepay — multi-entity holdback & VAT timing

Samantha —

Thanks, and appreciate the PO. Attached is a first-pass invoice schedule (RW_Proposed_Invoice_Schedule.csv) outlining:
- Initial up-front tranche (30%) wired to RDW US lockbox to start provisioning
- Monthly phased drawdowns over 9 months (40% total) released on milestone attestations
- Final holdback (30%) held for 90 days post-launch for usage true-up and SLA acceptance

Key tax/jurisdiction notes:
- EU VAT reclaim: we recommend invoicing the EU legal entity monthly with a reclaim window of 60 days after each invoice date — this aligns with most reclaim processors we've worked with.
- To avoid cross-entity VAT friction, we can route the EU invoices to your EU lockbox (instructions in RDW_lockbox_instructions.pdf).

Next steps:
1) Kimberly — can you confirm VAT reclaim window and whether we should shorten the holdback in jurisdictions with faster reclaim?
2) Vivek — can you validate the drawdown telemetry (we need the webhook/feed to push consumption to Brightlane ledger) — I cc'd Priyom for ops.
3) Samantha — please confirm bank details in the PO match the lockbox routing or if AP needs a different remit.

Happy to hop on a 30-min call if helpful.

Thanks,
Jordan Blake
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
[sig] Redwood Inference | jordan.blake@redwood.com

Attachments: RW_Proposed_Invoice_Schedule.csv (spreadsheet)
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 16 Mar 2027 09:21:00 -0700
Subject: Internal: draft schedule + telemetry spec request

Kimberly / Vivek / Priyom —

Copying the schedule I sent to Brightlane. I want your confirmation on two operational points before I finalize:
- VAT reclaim window: I proposed 60 days for EU; is 45 viable for UK entities? Any daylight risk if we push to 45?
- Drawdown telemetry: Brightlane wants near-real-time consumption so they can pull tranches monthly. Priyom, can the telemetry spec (attached) support an hourly push and a daily consolidated file for AP reconciliation?
- Lockbox routing: if we route initial tranche to RDW US and subsequent EU invoices to their EU lockbox, do we need additional intercompany netting steps?

I attached a short spec for the telemetry feed (drawdown_telemetry_spec.md). If we can confirm today I’ll update the CSV and send doc links to Brightlane.

Jordan

Attachments: drawdown_telemetry_spec.md (text)

Quoted message (from Samantha Price):

> Thanks for the quick sync last week. Brightlane is finalizing the legal ops for our committed prepay (RDW-4721) and we need a tight invoice & drawdown plan that handles...

Date: Wed, 17 Mar 2027 08:37:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Internal: draft schedule + telemetry spec request

Jordan / team —

Quick responses:
- EU VAT reclaim window: 60 days is conservative and safe; UK teams typically clear in ~45 days but that depends on their reclaim vendor. If Brightlane confirms a UK reclaim vendor, we can map UK invoices to 45 days.
- Holdback: Instead of a flat 30% final holdback, propose tiered holdbacks by jurisdiction: 20% (US), 25% (UK), 30% (EU) — that makes the economics clearer for AP and keeps the EU holdback aligned with longer reclaim cycles.
- Intercompany netting: to avoid double invoicing complexity we should implement a monthly netting file generated by our ledger team. Priyom, can you sign off on a CSV layout (invoice_id, entity_from, entity_to, net_amount, vat_id, month) and a scheduled drop on the 5th of each month to Brightlane?

I also attached a short lockbox instruction doc (RDW_lockbox_instructions.pdf) that lists the routing and beneficiary info — please use that when finalizing the invoice.

Next: Jordan, send the updated CSV to Samantha with the split holdbacks and the netting cadence. I’ll copy legal if Brightlane asks for contract language around holdback release conditions.

Thanks,
Kimberly Park
Head of Revenue Operations, Redwood Inference
[sig] kimberly.park@redwood.com

Attachments: RDW_lockbox_instructions.pdf (pdf)

Jordan / Kimberly —

Thanks — this looks good and aligned with internal timing. Two confirmations from our side:
1) We can accept tiered holdbacks as proposed (US 20% / UK 25% / EU 30%).
2) Our UK reclaim vendor can meet 45-day windows; EU reclaim will be ~60 days.

We’ll proceed with the initial wire to the US lockbox on 3/25 once we receive the final invoice CSV and the netting file layout. Please send the final schedule and the monthly netting CSV template by EOD tomorrow.

Best,
Samantha Price
VP Finance, Brightlane
